name: commutation.matrix
title: Commutation matrix for r by c numeric matrices

origin.description: This function returns a square matrix of order p = r * c that, for an r by c matrix A, transforms vec(A) to vec(A') where prime denotes transpose.
origin.details: If either argument is less than 2, or is not an integer, the function stops with an error message.
origin.example: K <- commutation.matrix(3, 4); A <- matrix(seq(1, 12, 1), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE); vecA <- vec(A); vecAt <- vec(t(A)); print(K %*% vecA); print(vecAt)

translation.description: This function returns a square matrix of order p = r * c that, for an r by c matrix A, transforms vec(A) to vec(A.T) with column-major vectorization like R.

arguments.name: c
arguments.text: A positive integer column dimension; defaults to r.

translation.details: If either argument is less than 2, or is not an integer, the function stops with an error message.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixcalc.commutation_matrix import commutation_matrix
K = commutation_matrix(3, 4)
A = np.arange(1, 13, dtype=float).reshape(3, 4, order="C")
vec_a = A.reshape(-1, order="F")
vec_at = A.T.reshape(-1, order="F")
print(K @ vec_a)
print(vec_at)
